::::: {.blog-docs}

## One scientific runtime per site build

The renderer combines core packages with the additional packages needed by posts that may execute. It then starts one shared Pixi environment for the site build.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Packages needed by documents that may execute are merged into one Pixi call."
flowchart TD
    A["Nix-pinned<br/>tools"] --> B["render-site.py"]
    C["Core packages"] --> D["Collect package specs"]
    E["Post A<br/>ci-packages"] --> D
    F["Post B<br/>ci-packages"] --> D
    B --> D
    D --> G{"Different constrained specs<br/>for the same package?"}
    G -->|Yes| X["Stop with error"]
    G -->|No| H["pixi exec"]
    H --> I["One Quarto render"]
```

## Document metadata

`ci-packages` is a **repository-specific field**, not built-in Quarto configuration.

```yaml
---
title: "Spatial Analysis"
ci-packages:
  - r-sf
  - r-spdep
  - "numpy>=1.26,<2"
---
```

`render-site.py` validates each list before passing the collected specifications to Pixi. Identical specifications are deduplicated. A version constraint takes precedence over a package name with no constraint.

Two different constrained specifications for the same package are rejected, even if their version ranges overlap. For example, `numpy>=1.26` and `numpy>=1.26,<2` cause an error. The script does not calculate their intersection; authors must use the same specification across posts. Pixi then resolves the accepted specifications together with their dependencies.

## Inspect the environment

The commands below use the repository's Nix shell, which currently supports `x86_64-linux`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Pinned tools

```bash
nix develop -c python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

Nix supplies Quarto, Pixi, Git and a Python YAML/testing environment.

### Shared R/Python runtime

```text
Core: R + knitr + reticulate + Python + NumPy
      + Pandoc + Micromamba compatibility executable
Additional: ci-packages from non-reused articles
                    ↓
One conda-forge pixi exec environment
```

The Micromamba executable serves as a compatibility tool for `reticulate`. It is not used to create a separate project environment.

### Dry run

```bash
nix develop -c python scripts/render-site.py --dry-run
```

This reports inspected documents, package specifications and the proposed render command without executing it.

:::

## What is skipped when a post is unchanged?

When the QMD source hash matches `scripts/freeze-manifest.json` **and** the saved HTML execution result exists, the renderer omits that post's extra `ci-packages`. The default R/Python toolchain still remains.

::: {.callout-important}
The manifest determines **dependency selection**, not Quarto execution directly. Deleting only the manifest may install extra packages without causing Quarto to recompute unchanged frozen results.
:::

| Design choice | Benefit | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| One `pixi exec` | Single render and common runtime | Different constrained specifications for the same package must be reconciled before the build |
| `ci-packages` per QMD | Requirements visible next to analysis | Authors must maintain metadata |
| Nix `flake.lock` | Pinned build tool versions | Doesn't lock the Pixi runtime |
| Frozen results | Avoids unnecessary computation | External changes need manual invalidation |
